recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-11004; related SDC profile cardinality decisions should remain in the SDC specification context.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core issue asking whether Questionnaire.subjectType and QuestionnaireResponse.subject are the same; the resolution required clarifying QuestionnaireResponse.subject so that, when a Questionnaire declares subjectType, the referenced subject resource must be an instance of that type.
initial_application: Historical commit 76675fcc91938801ee4e8de9ec10d2c6e1949bc8 explicitly listed QuestionnaireResponse #11004 and added the subjectType comment to the then-authoritative QuestionnaireResponse spreadsheet source. Later source migrations preserved the clarification in the current StructureDefinition XML.
additional_context: Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse are active resources in source/fhir.ini. Current Questionnaire.subjectType is repeatable and says omitted subjectType means the subject is unlimited; current QuestionnaireResponse.subject says the subject must be one of the listed types when subjectType is declared. Later SDC issue FHIR-27844 and associated minutes support this distinction, while FHIR-33171 concerns SDC profile behavior outside this FHIR-core reconciliation.
reconciliation: No source change was made because source/questionnaireresponse/structuredefinition-QuestionnaireResponse.xml already contains the requested clarification, and its plural wording is more accurate for the current 0..* Questionnaire.subjectType cardinality than the Jira resolution's original singular wording.

related_jiras.note: Later SDC decision relaxed subjectType cardinality and confirmed the distinction between Questionnaire allowed subject types and QuestionnaireResponse actual subject.
Later SDC profile issue adjusted QuestionnaireResponse profile subject expectations, but it is outside the FHIR-core source scope for FHIR-11004.
